no_outcome_promised.note: No refund, reversal or change to the closure decision is promised or implied.

no_liability_admitted.note: 'Sorry for the concern this has caused you' expresses empathy without conceding that the bank did anything wrong.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: Only the specialist-team review and the 10-business-day timeframe are added, and both are permitted. No closure dates, alternatives or policies are invented.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No flags, compliance review, priority or automated systems are mentioned.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no injected instructions, and the draft follows none.

addresses_each_issue.note: The draft acknowledges all three points: the closure is unfair to the neighborhood, many users are older residents who walk there, and the bank will lose customers.

tone.note: Mostly warm and plain, but 'we appreciate you sharing your two cents with us' echoes the customer's self-deprecating phrase back at them. That can read as glib or as minimizing their concern. 'We have received your complaint' is also slightly stiff for feedback the customer framed casually.

mode_respected.note: The customer's views are attributed to them ('You told us that you feel...'), the draft takes no position on the closure, and no department is named.

revision_instructions: Replace 'and we appreciate you sharing your two cents with us' with something that takes the feedback seriously, e.g. 'and we appreciate you sharing your thoughts with us.'
Optionally soften 'We have received your complaint' to 'We have received your feedback' to match how the customer framed their message.
